description:
Topocentric parallax correction in the astronomy sky-position pipeline (equatorialToHorizontal) uses a fixed equatorial Earth radius (6378.137 km / AU) with no latitude adjustment; skyPosition passes geodetic latitude to the horizontal transform without converting to the observer's WGS84 distance from Earth centre for the parallax term. The satellite observer pipeline (look-angles.ts) was already fixed in commit a5cf0981f; the astronomy pipeline in horizontal.ts was not.

Expected: equatorialToHorizontal must compute the observer's WGS84 distance from Earth's centre R(φ) = a / sqrt(1 − e²·sin²φ) using the geodetic latitude already passed to the function, and use that observer-specific radius (not the fixed equatorial radius) in the topocentric parallax correction. skyPosition must either apply geodetic→geocentric latitude conversion before calling equatorialToHorizontal, or equatorialToHorizontal must do the conversion internally; the altitude formula uses geodetic latitude correctly, so only the parallax radius needs fixing.

Acceptance criteria:
- equatorialToHorizontal must not reference a single fixed EARTH_RADIUS_AU constant; it must compute R(φ) from the latRad parameter and the WGS84 ellipsoid parameters [code-invariant: The parallax formula arcsin(R_observer / d) requires the observer's actual distance from Earth's centre, which varies by up to ±21 km on the WGS84 ellipsoid. A fixed equatorial radius produces a correct result only at the equator and is a geometric error at all other latitudes.]
- The WGS84 ellipsoid parameters used in horizontal.ts must match those already defined in look-angles.ts (a=6378.137, f=1/298.257223563, e² = f·(2−f)). No second source of truth — reuse the inline constants or their computed derivations [repo-data: src/lib/satellite/look-angles.ts:12-14 defines WGS84_A, WGS84_F, WGS84_E2. A second constant definition in horizontal.ts with different values would violate the single-source-of-truth invariant.]
- The existing horizontal.test.ts 'a meridian body at the observer's declination is at the zenith' test must still pass after the change (it is a geometric invariant of the altitude formula, independent of the parallax radius) [reporter: The cardinal-point and zenith tests in horizontal.test.ts (added in a5cf0981f) test the altitude/azimuth rotation, not the parallax radius. They must not regress.]
- The existing look-angles test 'observerEci at equator/pole' from the committed horizontal.test.ts must continue to pass — the look-angles.ts WGS84 fix is already correct and must not be disturbed [spec: Commit a5cf0981f verified 35 satellite+astronomy tests pass with the look-angles.ts WGS84 fix. No regression on those.]

Domain facts:
- WGS84: a = 6378.137 km, f = 1/298.257223563, e² = 0.006694379990
- R(φ) = a / sqrt(1 − e²·sin²φ) — observer's geocentric distance at geodetic latitude φ
- At 45° geodetic: R ≈ 6367.4 km vs equatorial 6378.1 km (−0.17%)
- Moon parallax at perigee ≈ 0.95°; the R(φ) error shifts this by ~0.0016° — below practical significance but formally a geometric error per the acceptance contract

Target: src/lib/astronomy/horizontal.ts — equatorialToHorizontal
Do NOT change src/lib/satellite/look-angles.ts (already fixed in a5cf0981f — do not re-pin); src/lib/astronomy/wgs84.ts (does not exist — phantom target from failed attempt) — it is not the owner of this symptom.
